definitions.gloss: detour, side trip, stopping by on the way
definitions.explanation: Making a stop at a place that is not one's main destination while on the way somewhere. Can also be used figuratively for getting sidetracked from a main task or topic.

examples.japanese: {帰|かえ}りに{寄|よ}り{道|みち}した。
examples.english: I made a stop on the way home.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{帰|かえ}りに{寄|よ}り{道|みち}しないで{帰|かえ}りなさい。
examples.english: Come straight home from school without making any detours.

examples.japanese: {出張|しゅっちょう}の{帰|かえ}りに{京都|きょうと}で{寄|よ}り{道|みち}して、{観光|かんこう}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: On the way back from a business trip, I made a side trip to Kyoto and enjoyed some sightseeing.

notes:
USAGE:
A warm, everyday word. Parents commonly tell children {寄|よ}り{道|みち}しないで (don't make detours / come straight home). Also used figuratively: {話|はなし}が{寄|よ}り{道|みち}する (the conversation goes off on a tangent). The word conveys a casual, unhurried feeling — the detour is usually for pleasure or curiosity rather than necessity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寄|よ}り{道|みち}する: to make a detour, to stop by
- {寄|よ}り{道|みち}しないで: without making detours
- {帰|かえ}りに{寄|よ}り{道|みち}する: to stop somewhere on the way home
- ちょっと{寄|よ}り{道|みち}: a little side trip
